Humanoids

Hallym tests a Blue Robin prototype in a simulated hospital ward

A wheeled, human-shaped prototype is being tested for corridor navigation and deliveries, rather than live patient service.

Health Chosun ↗20 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

The new development

Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital said on November 20 that it had tested an early robot prototype developed with Blue Robin at the Hallym Simulation Center. Recreated patient rooms and corridors help identify requirements before a robot enters a working hospital environment.

Technology and applications

The prototype combines a human-shaped upper body with a wheeled base. Tests examine narrow-space navigation, delivery of medical supplies and patient gowns, and movement of mobile equipment. Particular attention goes to crossing paths with people and the precision needed to pick up and deliver items.

Scope and next steps

Medical staff define tasks and requirements, with results feeding into hardware and software revisions. The focus is reducing walking and routine support work, not performing procedures directly on patients. No quantified success rate or commercial timetable was provided; simulated-ward testing should not be confused with live patient service.
